epic.title: Decision Tier Rebalance and Policy-Derived Trusted Autonomy
epic.description: Restore the repository-canonical decision-governance program to the live backlog and complete the remaining bridge from governed WWMD/WWWD/WSID judgment to scoped action authority. The program treats explicit yes as derived human approval only when standing policy, owning scope, evidence freshness, autonomy quality, work shape, and action/subject/organization/artifact bindings all agree; explicit no denies; the 'messy maybe' band routes bounded evidence-changing retry or human resolution. It also governs decision-vector adequacy, policy/weight lifecycle, regulator-grade traceability, and the TAK/JSI public account of the mechanism.
epic.scopeRationale: Universal platform governance and AI-agent decision authority across all organizations and work shapes; not customer-business logic.

items.title: Governed policy and weight lifecycle for narrowing the messy-maybe band safely
items.body:
## Problem
The three-band verdict, stakes-sensitive edges, real-margin persistence, bounded retry, reversal-rate telemetry, and weight inference have shipped. The remaining systemic requirement is a controlled lifecycle that uses those signals to improve criteria and weights without merely shrinking the middle band until it stops firing.

## Scope
Compose the shipped three-band decision verdict, DecisionInteraction chain, evidence reverification, corpus drift, WeightAdjustmentProposal, work-shape posture, and policy versioning. No second scoring engine.

## Acceptance
- Review populations are defined by owning scope, decision class, risk/stakes, organization, profession, policy version, and work shape.
- Calibration reports margin distribution, messy-maybe rate, reversal/error rate in both outer bands, evidence/corpus gaps, conflicts, overrides, outcome quality, and drift.
- A narrower middle band may be promoted only when outer-band reliability remains within an approved error budget; optimizing escalation count alone is prohibited.
- Weight or criterion changes travel through proposal -> review -> ratification -> effective window -> supersession/revocation, with before/after versions and replayable evaluations.
- Protected or regulated domains can set stricter review cadence, immutable floors, and dual-control triggers.
- Historical decisions are evaluated under the policy version actually used, not silently rescored as if the new policy had always applied.

## Dependencies
Blocked by: Universal policy-authority bridge.
Extends shipped three-band work (BI-2107B5D2 / PRs #4427, #4430, #4447) and weight inference (BI-D88DFEEA).

items.title: Universal policy-authority bridge from WWMD/WWWD/WSID verdicts to scoped action warrants
items.body:
## Problem
DPF can record high-quality DecisionInteraction judgments but cannot yet project a qualifying owning-scope verdict into action-specific authority. The current initiative-readiness defect is the first concrete failure: an explicit, autonomy-eligible policy yes is auditable but cannot lawfully authorize the bounded action without a new human approval loop.

## Scope
Extend the existing DecisionInteraction, WorkCasePolicyEnvelope, ReceiptEnvelope, AuthorizationDecisionLog, Principal/Organization, and coworker authority-gate substrate. Do not treat DecisionInteraction as RBAC and do not create a parallel approval table.

## Acceptance
- Explicit yes/proceed authorizes only when the owning WWMD/WWWD/WSID scope is correct, signalQuality.autonomyEligible is true, evidence is fresh, no commandment/conflict veto exists, and the standing-policy version, human root, organization, principal/delegation chain, work shape, action, subject, artifact, constraints, expiry, and revocation conditions all match.
- Explicit no/decline denies. Uncertain/defer/escalate/tie/stale/missing/corpus-gap enters the "messy maybe" path: bounded input-changing retry or human resolution.
- The action-specific writer atomically persists the authority projection and the resulting action receipt; it cannot be fabricated through caller-supplied organization or DecisionInteraction ids.
- A second human is required only when standing policy, regulation, risk floor, irreversible/outbound consequence, or commandment conflict explicitly requires dual control.
- Every allow is single-use or explicitly reusable by policy, expiring, revocable, and replay-safe.
- Conformance covers all three owning judgment scopes and direct-DI-as-RBAC prohibition.

## Dependencies
Blocked by: BI-F0715C9C (initiative-readiness bridge first slice).
Decisions: DI-053D69EADEDC, DI-568FF23AF27B, DI-6A25809B4683.

items.title: Publish the TAK/JSI article: From the messy maybe to policy-derived trusted autonomy
items.body:
## Outcome
Publish a reader-facing article and update the normative TAK/TAK-JSI references to explain DPF's policy-derived trusted-autonomy mechanism using this initiative-readiness episode as a transparent design case study.

## Required argument
- Human approval is invested first in standing policy, criteria, weights, authority scope, work shape, risk ceilings, and review cadence.
- WWMD, WWWD, and WSID are sibling owning judgment scopes.
- Explicit proceed/yes can become derived human approval only through the policy-authority bridge and exact action envelope.
- Explicit decline/no denies.
- The “messy maybe” is the narrow band for genuine trade-off, conflict, missing evidence, instability, or novelty; it triggers bounded evidence-changing retry or a human decision.
- The learning objective is to move well-understood cases toward reliable outer bands while measuring reversals and harms, not to manufacture certainty by narrowing thresholds.
- Workrooms give this mechanism its work shape, participants, action envelope, stop conditions, and receipts.
- JSI supplies job-specific criteria and qualification; TAK mediates runtime authority; GAID/Principal chains identify actors; DecisionInteraction preserves judgment; AuthorizationDecisionLog/receipts prove permitted action.
- DPF currently uses normalized weighted-sum MCDA over decision vectors. AHP eigenvectors are a proposed cold-start weight-elicitation technique, not the current runtime math.
- In hiring, proving race was not directly used is valuable but insufficient: proxy screening, outcome bias audits, lawful protected-class monitoring, and appeal are also required.

## Deliverables
- A public article under the existing architecture/standards publication structure.
- Targeted amendments to docs/architecture/trusted-ai-kernel.md, job-specific-intelligence.md, vector-decisioning-and-jsi.md, autonomy-and-wwmd.md, work-shapes-and-the-decision-gate.md, TAK/JSI conformance tests, and the standards white paper, using pointers rather than duplicate normative text.
- A diagram: standing policy -> owning judgment -> three bands -> scoped warrant -> action receipt -> outcome/recalibration.
- External standards citations and an explicit “implemented vs proposed” register.

## Dependencies
Blocked by: bootstrap bridge design stabilization; implementation claims must wait for shipped evidence.
Decisions: DI-053D69EADEDC, DI-568FF23AF27B, DI-6A25809B4683.

items.title: Regulator-grade decision evidence and fairness assertions across consequential domains
items.body:
## Problem
A regulator needs reproducible evidence of what criteria, inputs, policies, authorities, and models affected an autonomous action. Showing that race was not a direct scoring axis proves non-use of race itself; it does not by itself prove absence of proxy discrimination or disparate impact.

## Scope
Generalize the shipped Trust Envelope, DecisionInteraction hash chain, EvidenceReVerification, candidate-evaluation protected-axis/proxy screening, and DecisionBiasAuditMetric into a cross-domain conformance/export profile.

## Acceptance
- A decision evidence package records all candidate options, scored and excluded axes, raw-to-derived feature provenance, missingness, transformations, policy/principle/corpus versions, weights, evidence grades and locators, model/provider/version, prompts/instructions by digest, identities/authority chain, work shape, band edges, margin/cause, action warrant, receipt, and observed outcome.
- It distinguishes: not collected, collected but prohibited, available but unused, used directly, derived, and excluded after screening.
- Protected-characteristic non-use is a precise assertion, never overclaimed as proof of no bias.
- Regulated profiles add proxy screening, subgroup outcome/selection-rate analysis where lawful, adverse-impact thresholds, counterfactual or matched testing where appropriate, accessibility review, and documented human appeal/remediation.
- Exports are tamper-evident, reproducible, retention-aware, privacy-minimized, jurisdiction-tagged, and independently verifiable.
- Missing provenance, stale evidence, unexplained proxy risk, or failed impact thresholds prevents an outer-band autonomous assurance.

## Dependencies
Blocked by: Universal policy-authority bridge; composes existing Trust Envelope implementation (PR #4059).

items.title: AHP pairwise elicitation as a cold-start input to the governed weight proposal ladder
items.body:
## Problem
New organizations and job profiles lack enough historical rulings for revealed-preference inference. Asking a non-technical operator to author raw numeric weights is fragile.

## Scope
Add Saaty-style pairwise comparison only as a cold-start elicitation method feeding the existing WeightAdjustmentProposal lifecycle. It is not a new scorer, authority model, or permission grant; DPF's runtime option scoring remains normalized weighted-sum MCDA.

## Acceptance
- The operator compares a bounded, job-relevant criterion set with a documented intensity scale.
- The system derives a candidate weight vector and reports consistency ratio, inconsistent comparisons, sensitivity, and the evidence/author identity.
- Inconsistent or underdetermined results remain messy-maybe and cannot become action authority.
- The result enters the existing proposal/review/ratification lifecycle at an explicitly unconfirmed confidence tier.
- No new spine axis can be created by elicitation; profession-local axes must already be governed and project to the spine.
- Public docs use “eigenvector” only for this genuine AHP derivation, not as a synonym for DPF decision dimensions.

## Dependencies
Blocked by: Decision-vector adequacy and job-specific criterion inventory.
Source: docs/architecture/vector-decisioning-and-jsi.md §4 and docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-external-vector-decisioning-writeup-validation.md.

items.title: Demand scoring judges the effort estimate by provenance, not evidence
items.body:
## Problem

Two rules in demand scoring decide an effort estimate's standing by who produced it rather than what grounds it. Both contradict AGENTS.md section 12: "Governance approves evidence, not provenance — the keystone. A gate reads its required evidence fields; it never asks which surface produced them." They also sit against the commandment "Do the work; don't task the operator with what an agent can do."

**1. An AI estimate is provisional by provenance.** `apps/web/lib/demand/activation.ts:105`

```
const provisional =
  input.estimateDiverged ||
  input.estimateSource === "ai" ||
  (input.estimateSource !== null && input.estimateAgreed === false);
```

The second clause needs no disagreement and no divergence. An estimate is unusable because an AI made it. `provisional` blocks `scoreReady`, which blocks `fundingReady`, which blocks the funnel to `ready` — so every AI-estimated item stalls until a human clicks confirm.

**2. A human number unconditionally overrules an AI one.** `apps/web/lib/demand/estimate-provenance.ts:94`

```
// Human overrules AI; otherwise whichever single side estimated.
const effectiveJobSize = human !== null ? human : ai;
```

Not on better grounding. Not on cited evidence. On being human.

## Why this is wrong on the merits

`jobSize` here is a technical complexity measurement. The AI estimator reads the actual schema, migration surface and test surface. A reviewer who has not read them holds strictly less information, so the confirmation cannot be a judgement — it can only be a rubber stamp. Ceremony that presents itself as governance is worse than no gate: it manufactures assurance nobody actually supplied.

The genuinely human judgement in this funnel is appetite and priority — what the business chooses to spend on. That is already a separate, correctly-human blocker (`validBucket`, the investment bucket). The defect is conflating a measurement with a decision and asking the wrong party to confirm the measurement.

## Expected vs actual

Expected: an estimate stands on its recorded grounding; disagreement between two estimates is the exception that needs reconciliation.
Actual: an AI-sourced estimate is permanently provisional, and any human number silently wins.

## Suggested fix

- Drop the `estimateSource === "ai"` clause from `provisional`. Keep `estimateDiverged` — a competing number is a real signal.
- Replace "human overrules AI" with symmetric divergence handling: neither side wins by provenance; a divergence is reconciled on stated grounds.
- Keep the investment-bucket blocker exactly as it is. That decision is the human's and should stay.
- Add a test asserting that an estimate with identical grounding scores identically regardless of `estimateSource`, so this cannot regress.

## Scale

Affects every backlog item on every installation that is estimated by an agent, which under an AI-native operating model is the default path rather than an edge case. Observed on all seven items of EP-862820FD, each reporting "Confirm or overrule the proposed AI effort estimate" with `estimateAgreed: false` despite complete score inputs.

## Founder position

Raised 2026-08-26: humans are not qualified to override an AI effort estimate, so the ask is irrational. Verified against the code above; the position is correct and is already platform doctrine in section 12.

items.title: Decision-vector adequacy and job-specific criterion inventory for JSI
items.body:
## Problem
Trusted autonomy depends on capturing enough materially distinct decision dimensions to discriminate alternatives. The platform has a closed shared spine and profession-local projection substrate, but the job-specific inventories remain incomplete and coverage can be concentrated on too few axes.

## Scope
Implement the repository-canonical design in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-job-specific-decision-vector-inventory-design.md. Reuse PRINCIPLE_DIMENSIONS, dimension scope/projection, profession corpora, evidence grades, and revealed-preference proposals.

## Acceptance
- Each decision class declares a versioned criterion inventory: required axes, optional axes, cost/benefit sign, source/owner, evidence expectations, applicable scope, proxy/protected-feature restrictions, and projection to the shared spine.
- Adequacy checks detect missing required criteria, weak discrimination, rank deficiency, over-concentration, contradictory criteria, and options not assessed on comparable evidence.
- Missing or contradictory material yields messy-maybe rather than confident zero.
- Profession-local JSI axes remain namespaced and project to the shared spine; organizations reweight governed axes rather than inventing fleet-fragmenting private dimensions.
- Corpus mining, external professional standards, prior decisions, and outcome evidence are distinguished and cited.
- At least three deep professions are inventoried and measured before fleet expansion.

## Dependencies
May proceed after the bridge contract is stable; feeds policy calibration and article evidence.
